How to confirm console settings access (self-check)
- Verify your IAM role and permissions:
  - Check that you are assigned to a role/group with Console Management or Console Settings permissions.
  - Confirm you have at least view rights to Console Settings, and ideally modify rights only if you’re authorized.
- Confirm authentication requirements:
  - Ensure MFA is enabled and your session/token is active.
  - Check the last successful login and current token validity in the identity portal.
- Review access scope:
  - Look for permissions related to: Console Settings, Overrides management, Audit logs access, and any maintenance window controls.
- Check audit/logs:
  - Verify there are no pending approval requirements for your access, and review recent changes or attempted changes to console settings.

If you want to proceed without risking misconfigurations
- I can draft a formal request to your IT/Security team to confirm or grant console access. You can then sign and submit it. Below is a ready-to-use template you can adapt.

Draft: Access Confirmation Request for Console Settings
- To: IT Security / Identity & Access Management
- Subject: Confirmation of Console Settings Access for [Your Name], [Role]
- Body:
  - Please confirm the current access level for [Your Name], [Role], in the operations console.
  - Specifically, confirm whether the user has:
    - Read-only access to Console Settings
    - Modify/Manage access to Console Settings
    - Permissions to initiate and approve overrides (e.g., SYNC_DATA_OVERRIDE, TEMP_MAINTENANCE_OVERRIDE, ACCESS_LOG_PURGE)

  - If access is not currently granted, please provide the steps and timeframe to obtain the appropriate authorization, including any required approvals and temporary access options.

- Signature: [Your signature]
- Deadline: [Optional]

If you’d like, tell me:
- Your name and role
- The exact console settings areas you need access to (read vs. modify)
- Any compliance or time window requirements

Would you like me to:
- Walk you through a step-by-step in your system, if you describe your UI, or
- Prepare and format the access confirmation request for you to submit?

- Roles (participants)
  - Operator on duty, Shift Lead, Control Room Manager, Safety Officer, IT/Security liaison, Audit/compliance representative.
  - Observers and scribe(s) for logs and decision capture.

- Timeline and cadence
  - Tabletop-first (60–90 minutes) to validate decisions and documentation.
  - If available, a shadow-run in a digital twin (2–3 hours) to validate data flows and dashboards with synthetic data.

- Success criteria
  - All readiness items are addressed and documented.
  - Mock approvals are obtained in the simulation and logged.
  - A complete, non-operational audit trail is generated.
  - Gaps are identified with owners and due dates for closure.

- Objective, scope, environment, participants, scenario catalog, success criteria, and exit criteria.

2) Mock Emergency Override Authorization Request (simulation)

- Body: includes Requestor, System/Area, Override, Simulated Justification, Urgency, Scope, Duration, Risk Mitigation, Backout, Required Approvals, Signatures (placeholders)

3) Pre-override Readiness Checklist (simulation data)
- Incident/State: simulated interlock health
- Critical subsystems affected: list
- Justification and urgency: short description
- Estimated duration: time window
- Approvers available: names/roles
- Monitoring and logging: dashboards and log targets
- Backout/rollback: simulated criteria
- Stakeholders: notify list

4) Tabletop Exercise Script (simulation prompts)
- Start with a safety disclaimer: no live overrides will be triggered.
- Role prompts and decision points: justification, approvals, scope, monitoring, rollback, documentation.
- Debrief prompts: gaps, action owners, due dates.

5) Post-Drill Debrief and Action-Item Tracker
- Questions to surface improvements, owners, and timelines.

- Your name and role (for signatures and context)
- Subsystems to include in the drill (e.g., interlocks, data paths, resource management, logging)
- Drill duration and whether you prefer tabletop only or digital twin shadow-run
- Mock approvers (names, roles, contact methods)
- Confirmation that you have a safe, isolated test/digital twin environment

Next steps (ready-to-run deliverables)
- If you provide the specifics above, I will generate:
  - A complete EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE_ACT non-activating simulation package (Run Plan, Mock Authorization Request, Readiness Checklist, Exercise Script, Debrief template)

I’ll produce the full non-activating simulation package immediately.
